questions.sub_topic: Harappan Civilisation and Archaeology
questions.question: Which mythical or real animal is most frequently engraved on standard square steatite Harappan seals?
questions.explanation: The single-horned mythical animal (commonly termed the 'unicorn') is the most ubiquitous motif on Harappan stamp seals.

questions.sub_topic: Harappan Civilisation and Archaeology
questions.question: In Mesopotamian texts, which island trading hub situated in the Persian Gulf was referred to as 'Dilmun'?
questions.explanation: Dilmun is universally identified by historians with the island of Bahrain in the Persian Gulf.

questions.sub_topic: Political and Economic Systems in Early States: Inscriptional Evidences
questions.question: Which of the following was NOT among the sixteen Mahajanapadas listed in early Buddhist and Jaina sources?
questions.explanation: Pataliputra was an imperial capital city, not an independent Mahajanapada (the state was Magadha).

questions.sub_topic: Political and Economic Systems in Early States: Inscriptional Evidences
questions.question: Which Chinese pilgrim visited India during the reign of the Gupta dynasty (c. early 5th century CE) and wrote detailed notes on society and monasteries?
questions.explanation: Faxian travelled to India during the reign of Chandragupta II Vikramaditya to collect authentic Buddhist Vinaya texts.

questions.sub_topic: Social Histories of Early Societies: Mahabharata
questions.question: In the game of dice in the Mahabharata, who played on behalf of Duryodhana against Yudhishthira using loaded dice?
questions.explanation: Shakuni, the maternal uncle of the Kauravas, manipulated the game of dice to strip the Pandavas of their kingdom.

questions.sub_topic: History of Buddhism and Jainism: Cultural Developments
questions.question: The foundational philosophical sermons delivered by Vardhamana Mahavira are compiled in the canonical texts known as the:
questions.explanation: The Jain canonical literature consisting of the Angas and Upangas is collectively known as the Agamas, composed in Ardhamagadhi Prakrit.

questions.sub_topic: History of Buddhism and Jainism: Cultural Developments
questions.question: The hemispherical mound of earth forming the core of a Buddhist stupa is technically termed the:
questions.explanation: The anda (literally egg) is the semi-circular hemispherical earthen mound representing the cosmic vault in stupa architecture.

questions.sub_topic: Medieval Society through Travellers Accounts
questions.question: Sultan Mahmud of Ghazni brought Al-Biruni to his capital Ghazni in 1017 following his military invasion of:
questions.explanation: Mahmud of Ghazni invaded Khwarizm in 1017 and took several scholars and poets, including Al-Biruni, to Ghazni.

questions.sub_topic: Religious History: Bhakti-Sufi Traditions
questions.question: The famous Chishti Sufi dargah at Ajmer is dedicated to which venerated saint?
questions.explanation: The Ajmer dargah is the tomb-shrine of Khwaja Muinuddin Chishti (Gharib Nawaz), who settled there in the late 12th century.

questions.sub_topic: Vijayanagara Empire: Politics, Economy and Architecture
questions.question: In 1565, the armies of the Deccan Sultanates defeated Vijayanagara at the Battle of Talikota, which was fought near the twin villages of:
questions.explanation: The decisive battle of 1565 is known in local records as the Battle of Rakshasi-Tangadi, named after the two neighboring villages.

questions.sub_topic: The Mughal Empire and Agrarian Society
questions.question: Under the Ain-i-Akbari's land classification, land that was left fallow for a year or two in order to recover its natural fertility was termed:
questions.explanation: Parauti is land left out of cultivation for a short time (1 to 2 years) that it may recover its strength.

questions.sub_topic: Colonialism and Rural Society: Evidence from Official Reports
questions.question: The British Governor-General who presided over the enactment of the Permanent Settlement in Bengal in 1793 was:
questions.explanation: Lord Charles Cornwallis introduced the Permanent Settlement in Bengal, Bihar, and Orissa in 1793.

questions.sub_topic: Revolt of 1857: Patterns and Representations
questions.question: What religious issue concerning the cartridges of the newly introduced Enfield rifle sparked outrage among Hindu and Muslim sepoys in early 1857?
options: A) Greasing with cow and pig fat
B) Dipping cartridges in sheep blood
C) Packaging cartridges in animal intestines
D) Stamping cartridges with the British royal crest
questions.explanation: The cartridges were rumored to be greased with the fat of cows (sacred to Hindus) and pigs (forbidden to Muslims), which sepoys had to bite off.

questions.sub_topic: Mahatma Gandhi and National Movements
questions.question: On which date did Mahatma Gandhi arrive at the seashore village of Dandi and ceremonially break the salt law by picking up a lump of natural salt?
questions.explanation: Gandhiji arrived at Dandi on 5 April and formally manufactured salt in defiance of colonial law on the morning of 6 April 1930.

questions.sub_topic: The Making of the Constitution
questions.question: The historic 'Objectives Resolution' outlining the guiding principles of independent India's Constitution was introduced by:
questions.explanation: Jawaharlal Nehru moved the Objectives Resolution on 13 December 1946 in the Constituent Assembly.

questions.sub_topic: Harappan Civilisation and Archaeology
questions.question: Archaeologist Sir Mortimer Wheeler advanced the hypothesis in 1947 that the Indus Valley Civilization was destroyed by Aryan invaders, basing his argument primarily on:
options: A) Radio-carbon dates of charred wood at Harappa
B) Unburied human skeletons discovered in the lanes of Mohenjodaro and Rigvedic verses mentioning Indra destroying puras (forts)
C) Sanskrit inscriptions found engraved on bronze daggers at Lothal
D) Large iron sword blades excavated from the Citadel of Harappa
questions.explanation: Wheeler cited unburied skeletons at Mohenjodaro and Rigvedic references to Indra as 'Purandara' (fort-destroyer) to propose an Aryan conquest theory, later refuted.

questions.sub_topic: Political and Economic Systems in Early States: Inscriptional Evidences
questions.question: Which of the following Ashokan edicts discovered near Kandahar in southern Afghanistan was written in Greek and Aramaic scripts?
questions.explanation: The Shar-i-Kuna bilingual rock inscription discovered at Kandahar was composed in Greek and Aramaic for the local Hellenistic and Iranian populations.

questions.sub_topic: Social Histories of Early Societies: Mahabharata
questions.question: In the Mahabharata's Sabha Parva, what profound legal and moral question did Draupadi raise before the Kuru assembly when dragged into the court by Dushasana?
options: A) Why were the Pandavas denied their equal share of the royal cattle herds?
B) Did Yudhishthira lose himself first before staking her, or did he wager her while still a free man?
C) Why did Dhritarashtra refuse to abdicate the throne in favor of Bhishma?
D) What right had Shakuni to throw the dice on behalf of Gandhari?
questions.explanation: Draupadi famously challenged the court elders: if Yudhishthira had already lost himself and become an unfree slave, did he possess the legal right to stake his free wife?

questions.sub_topic: History of Buddhism and Jainism: Cultural Developments
questions.question: Which schism in the Jain community resulted in the division into the Digambaras (sky-clad ascetics) and Svetambaras (white-clad ascetics)?
options: A) Disagreement over the divinity of Parshvanatha
B) Debate over the necessity of wearing clothes and ascetic nudity
C) Rejection of non-violence (ahimsa) by northern monks
D) Disagreement regarding the adoption of Sanskrit over Prakrit
questions.explanation: The primary difference centered on whether complete renunciation required giving up all possessions including clothing (Digambara) or permitting white robes (Svetambara).

questions.sub_topic: Medieval Society through Travellers Accounts
questions.question: In Kitab-ul-Hind, Al-Biruni described the Indian system of numbers and place-value arithmetic, noting with admiration that:
options: A) Indian mathematicians used Greek roman numerals exclusively
B) The decimal system and the concept of zero originated in India and were adopted by the Arab world
C) Brahmagupta had translated Arabic algebra into Sanskrit
D) The decimal system was imported from China
questions.explanation: Al-Biruni studied and praised Indian decimal place-value numeration, which Arab scholars termed 'Hindsa' and transmitted to the West.

questions.sub_topic: Religious History: Bhakti-Sufi Traditions
questions.question: Which Bhakti mystic of northern India, born into a family of Muslim weavers (julahas) in Varanasi, preached devotion to a formless Absolute through his dohas?
questions.explanation: Kabir was brought up in a family of Muslim weavers (julahas) in Varanasi, composing verses in vernacular Hindavi expressing nirguna bhakti.

questions.sub_topic: Vijayanagara Empire: Politics, Economy and Architecture
questions.question: Which of the following reservoirs, constructed during the early fifteenth century, supplied water to both the agricultural fields and the Royal Centre of Vijayanagara?
questions.explanation: The Kamalapuram tank, built in the early 15th century, channeled water through stone conduits into the royal complex and surrounding gardens.

questions.sub_topic: The Mughal Empire and Agrarian Society
questions.question: In the Ain-i-Akbari, agricultural lands that lay uncultivated for three or four years were classified as:
questions.explanation: Chachar was land that had lain fallow for three or four years; banjar was uncultivated for five years and more.

questions.sub_topic: Colonialism and Rural Society: Evidence from Official Reports
questions.question: Why did the British administrators find the Paharias of the Rajmahal Hills extremely difficult to control and tax during the late eighteenth century?
options: A) They held modern artillery supplied by the French navy
B) They lived deep within the rugged jungle hills, maintained egalitarian autonomy, and conducted swift guerilla raids on plains settlements
C) They had formed an offensive military alliance with the Nawab of Awadh
D) They spoke a secret Persian cipher undecipherable by British collectors
questions.explanation: The Paharias retreated into dense forests, lived by hunting and shifting agriculture, and raided plains caravans, defying outside interference.

questions.sub_topic: Colonialism and Rural Society: Evidence from Official Reports
questions.question: In Bengal under the Permanent Settlement, what official power did the zamindar retain to recover defaulted rent from recalcitrant tenants?
options: A) Execution of the tenant by royal decree
B) Distraint of the tenant's crops and auctioning of their personal cattle
C) Exiling the tenant to the Andaman islands
D) Confiscation of the tenant's ancestral caste rank
questions.explanation: Under Regulation VII of 1799, zamindars were given summary powers of distraint (seizure) of crops and cattle to recover arrears from ryots.

questions.sub_topic: Revolt of 1857: Patterns and Representations
questions.question: During the 1857 Revolt, which rebel commander proclaimed himself the Peshwa at Kanpur and established an independent administration?
questions.explanation: Nana Sahib declared himself Peshwa, acknowledged Bahadur Shah Zafar as Emperor, and governed Kanpur until forced to flee.

questions.sub_topic: Mahatma Gandhi and National Movements
questions.question: At the Second Round Table Conference held in London in 1931, Mahatma Gandhi claimed that the Indian National Congress:
options: A) Was merely an advisory cultural association
B) Represented only the high-caste Hindu intelligentsia of Bombay and Bengal
C) Solely and exclusively represented the entire population of India, including all religious communities and depressed classes
D) Endorsed separate electorates for all minority groups
questions.explanation: Gandhiji asserted that Congress was the sole representative of all Indian interests, which was contested by the Muslim League, princely states, and Dr. Ambedkar.

questions.sub_topic: The Making of the Constitution
questions.question: In the Constituent Assembly, which distinguished member passionately advocated the adoption of Hindustani—a blend of Hindi and Urdu—as the national link language?
options: C) Mahatma Gandhi and Jawaharlal Nehru
questions.explanation: Gandhiji and Nehru championed Hindustani as a composite, inclusive bridge language easily understood by common Hindus and Muslims.

questions.sub_topic: Political and Economic Systems in Early States: Inscriptional Evidences
questions.question: In ancient Indian numismatics, who were the first rulers to issue gold coins in northern India featuring bilingual inscriptions and royal portraits?
questions.explanation: The Indo-Greeks were the first in the subcontinent to issue coins with the names and portraits of reigning kings.

questions.sub_topic: Religious History: Bhakti-Sufi Traditions
questions.question: Which Sikh Guru established the 'Khalsa Panth' (the Army of the Pure) at Anandpur Sahib on Baisakhi day in 1699?
questions.explanation: Guru Gobind Singh, the tenth Guru, founded the Khalsa Panth in 1699, giving Sikhs a distinct identity characterized by the Five Ks.

questions.sub_topic: Vijayanagara Empire: Politics, Economy and Architecture
questions.question: In the Hazara Rama temple at Vijayanagara, the sculpted narrative friezes carved into the outer stone walls illustrate scenes from which epic?
questions.explanation: The walls of the Hazara Rama temple are richly sculpted with narrative episodes from the Ramayana.

questions.sub_topic: Colonialism and Rural Society: Evidence from Official Reports
questions.question: The Santhal insurrection (Hul) of 1855 was ignited primarily because:
options: A) The Santhals were forced to convert to Christianity
B) The British banned the Santhal language in local markets
C) Moneylenders (dikus) charged exorbitant interest, British taxes escalated, and zamindars asserted control over the Damin-i-Koh
D) The East India Company closed all iron-ore mines in Chota Nagpur
questions.explanation: Santhals revolted because rapacious moneylenders (dikus), heavy British revenue demands, and encroaching zamindars drove them into deep debt.

questions.sub_topic: Mahatma Gandhi and National Movements
questions.question: The tragic incident of police firing and mob violence at Chauri Chaura occurred in Gorakhpur district on:
questions.explanation: On 4 February 1922, protesters set fire to the Chauri Chaura police post, prompting Gandhi to call off the Non-Cooperation Movement.

questions.sub_topic: The Making of the Constitution
questions.question: In the Constituent Assembly, which committee was responsible for defining the administrative relations and distribution of legislative powers between the Union and the States?
questions.explanation: The Union Powers Committee, chaired by Jawaharlal Nehru, formulated the distribution of powers across the Union, State, and Concurrent lists.

questions.sub_topic: Social Histories of Early Societies: Mahabharata
questions.question: According to ancient Sanskrit legal texts, what was the term for marriage within one's own kin group or caste unit?
questions.explanation: Endogamy refers to marriage within a unit (such as a kin group, caste, or locality); exogamy refers to marriage outside the unit.

questions.sub_topic: The Mughal Empire and Agrarian Society
questions.question: In the Ain-i-Akbari, what was the imperial revenue assessment system based on the actual measurement of cultivated land called?
questions.explanation: Under the Zabt or Zabti system, lands were systematically surveyed and measured with standard measuring rods, and revenue was assessed based on crop yields.

questions.sub_topic: Revolt of 1857: Patterns and Representations
questions.question: Which of the following British visual depictions of 1857 represented British vengeance by showing rebel sepoys being tied to the mouths of cannons and blown apart?
options: C) 'Blowing Mutineers from Guns' by Felice Beato and British prints
questions.explanation: Numerous contemporary British engravings depicted rebel prisoners being executed by blowing from cannons as imperial retribution.

questions.sub_topic: Mahatma Gandhi and National Movements
questions.question: In 1942, why did Mahatma Gandhi describe Sir Stafford Cripps' post-war constitutional proposal as a 'post-dated cheque on a crashing bank'?
options: A) Because the proposal rejected the formation of an Indian army
B) Because the British Treasury refused to honor Indian paper currency
C) Because it promised Dominion Status only after the uncertain conclusion of World War II, while retaining British military control and conceding the right of provinces to secede
D) Because Sir Stafford Cripps demanded immediate war indemnities from Indian taxpayers
questions.explanation: Gandhiji rejected Cripps' proposal because it delayed real independence until after the war and allowed provinces to secede, threatening India's unity.

questions.sub_topic: Harappan Civilisation and Archaeology
questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding the decipherment of the Harappan civilization's urban origins:
1. Early Harappan levels at Kot Diji, Amri, and Kalibangan reveal distinctive pottery styles, evidence of burning, and smaller defensive walls.
2. The transition to Mature Harappan urbanism is marked by the introduction of standardized bricks, specialized crafts, and street grid planning.
3. Harappan settlements completely lacked any agricultural implements made of flint or stone.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is incorrect because Harappans made extensive use of stone blades made of Rohri chert for harvesting.

questions.sub_topic: Political and Economic Systems in Early States: Inscriptional Evidences
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the administration of justice and public welfare under Ashoka's Dhamma is accurate based on his Pillar Edicts?
options: A) He prohibited the study of Sanskrit grammar in monasteries
B) He instituted mandatory capital punishment for all theft offenses
C) He ordered the closure of all public veterinary hospitals outside Pataliputra
D) He granted a three-day respite to prisoners sentenced to death so their kin could appeal or they could prepare their minds through meditation
questions.explanation: In Pillar Edict IV, Ashoka declared that prisoners condemned to death were granted three days' reprieve so relatives could plead for their lives or they could fast and meditate.

questions.sub_topic: Social Histories of Early Societies: Mahabharata
questions.question: How did Brahmanical Dharmashastras justify the absorption of non-Vedic tribal communities and specialized professional groups who did not fit the four varnas?
options: A) By denying them any legal or commercial standing
B) By exiling them permanently beyond the Himalayas
C) By forcibly converting them into Vedic priests
D) By categorizing them as distinct 'jatis' created through varna-samkara (intermixture of varnas)
questions.explanation: Dharmashastras integrated diverse social groups like Nishadas, goldsmiths (Suvarnakaras), and weavers into the social hierarchy by classifying them as jatis arising from inter-varna unions.

questions.sub_topic: History of Buddhism and Jainism: Cultural Developments
questions.question: In the evolution of Buddhist art, why did nineteenth-century European art historians initially fail to understand the symbolic meaning of early reliefs at Sanchi and Bharhut?
options: A) They assumed the stupas were military storehouses of the British army
B) The inscriptions were completely erased by monsoon rains
C) They believed the monuments were built by ancient Greeks from Alexandria
D) They searched for anthropomorphic statues of the Buddha and mistook aniconic symbols (the empty seat, umbrella, footprints, and stupa) as primitive pagan nature worship
questions.explanation: Early European scholars looked for human depictions of Buddha and misidentified symbolic motifs (trees, wheels, empty thrones) as tree-worship and animism before translating Buddhist texts.

questions.sub_topic: Medieval Society through Travellers Accounts
questions.question: What fundamental contradiction did Francois Bernier identify in the Mughal urban economy regarding the relationship between the artisan and the state?
options: A) Artisans could sell goods only to European trading ships
B) Artisans were prohibited from using silver coins in municipal markets
C) The state forced artisans to convert to Islam under penalty of exile
D) Despite producing world-class luxury goods in karkhanas, artisans had no economic incentive to improve technology because any accumulated wealth was seized by rapacious nobles
questions.explanation: Bernier observed that artisans had no motivation to innovate or display wealth, as arbitrary exactions by nobles kept them impoverished while their skills were exploited in royal karkhanas.

questions.sub_topic: Religious History: Bhakti-Sufi Traditions
questions.question:
Examine the following statements regarding the Chishti practice of 'Ziyarat' at the dargah of Shaikh Muinuddin Chishti in Ajmer:
1. Muhammad bin Tughlaq was the first Delhi Sultan to personally visit the shrine.
2. Emperor Akbar visited the shrine fourteen times between 1562 and 1579, often walking on foot from Agra.
3. Akbar donated a massive bronze cauldron (deg) to cook food for pilgrims at the dargah.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: All three statements are historically accurate: Muhammad bin Tughlaq was the first Sultan to visit, Akbar made 14 pilgrimages, and he gifted the famous monumental deg.

questions.sub_topic: Vijayanagara Empire: Politics, Economy and Architecture
questions.question: In the administrative structure of the Vijayanagara Empire, how did the central imperial authority ensure that the 'amara-nayakas' remained loyal and did not establish independent petty dynasties?
options: A) The nayakas were forbidden from collecting any land revenue directly
B) The kings retained the nayakas' eldest sons as royal hostages in the capital
C) The kings disbanded all provincial military garrisons every three years
D) The kings frequently transferred nayakas from one territory to another and required them to appear personally at court during the annual Mahanavami festival with tribute
questions.explanation: Rayas maintained control over amara-nayakas by transferring them across territories, receiving their annual tribute, and requiring their physical attendance during state festivals.

questions.sub_topic: The Mughal Empire and Agrarian Society
questions.question: Under the Ain-i-Akbari's fiscal regulations, how was the village accountant (patwari) held strictly accountable for revenue records?
options: A) He had to surrender half his family's annual income to the village headman
B) He had to deposit his personal land title as security with the provincial governor
C) He was forbidden from owning private agricultural land within ten kos of his village
D) He was required to maintain a daily journal of receipts and disbursements and furnish duplicate certified ledgers to the imperial pargana collector (amil)
questions.explanation: The patwari was legally obligated to maintain transparent, itemized ledgers (khasra and bahi) and submit synchronized duplicates to pargana officers.

questions.sub_topic: Colonialism and Rural Society: Evidence from Official Reports
questions.question: Which of the following was a direct social consequence of the Limitation Law of 1859 in the Bombay Deccan?
options: A) Ryots formed cooperative credit societies under British district collectors
B) All peasant debt contracts were canceled by the Bombay high court
C) Moneylenders ceased all lending operations in Poona and Ahmednagar districts
D) Moneylenders subverted the 3-year validity rule by forcing illiterate ryots to sign entirely new bonds every three years, adding accumulated unpaid interest to the new principal
questions.explanation: Rather than protecting ryots, the Limitation Law exacerbated debt; sahukars compounded unpaid interest into new principal bonds every 36 months, compounding peasant misery.

questions.sub_topic: Revolt of 1857: Patterns and Representations
questions.question: Why did the British annexation of Awadh in 1856 produce intense disaffection not merely among the royal court, but specifically among the common sepoys of the Bengal Army?
options: A) All sepoy pensions from Awadh were converted into British government bonds
B) The British lowered the salary of Awadh recruits by 50%
C) Sepoys from Awadh were forbidden from writing letters home
D) The sepoys, mostly recruited from Awadh villages, saw their sovereign dethroned, and their families back home were subjected to increased land revenue and harassment by British revenue courts
questions.explanation: Sepoys were 'peasants in uniform'; the dethronement of their Nawab and the Summary Settlement of 1856 dispossessed their families and taluqdars, generating deep collective resentment.

questions.sub_topic: Mahatma Gandhi and National Movements
questions.question: In his seminal 1909 treatise 'Hind Swaraj' (Indian Home Rule), Mahatma Gandhi argued that true self-rule (swaraj) required Indians to:
options: A) Form an international armed legion to overthrow European colonial powers
B) Build heavy industrial steel mills and steamship yards
C) Adopt British parliamentary institutions with universal franchise immediately
D) Renounce modern Western industrial civilization, machinery, and adversarial institutions, and cultivate moral self-mastery rooted in indigenous ethical values
questions.explanation: In Hind Swaraj, Gandhiji defined swaraj not merely as expelling the British, but as freeing India from the soul-destroying materialism, machinery, and moral decadence of Western civilization.

questions.sub_topic: The Making of the Constitution
questions.question: In the Constituent Assembly debates, who warned that 'We are going to enter into a life of contradictions. In politics we will have equality and in social and economic life we will have inequality', urging the eradication of social disparities?
questions.explanation: In his final speech to the Constituent Assembly on 25 November 1949, Dr. Ambedkar famously warned of the dangerous contradiction between political equality ('one man, one vote') and persistent socioeconomic inequality.
